title: perf-canary: add paging (Sev2/Sev1) alert rules for sustained per-model regressions
author: Allison Grant
description: Summary: This adds paging-tier perf-canary alert rules (Sev2 + Sev1) for sustained regressions on top models. These are intentionally stricter than the warning rules in pr-19179 (higher minimum sample size, longer sustain window, and stricter anti-flap) and route to the on-call rotation channel via incident-bot. Motivation: During phase-1 rollout we saw warning-level regressions that were actionable when they sustained (real tail-latency impact), but the existing rules were designed to be noisy-tolerant and non-paging. This PR implements the paging path that SRE approved in the paging policy thread and is required for rollout gates integration. Alerting model: We page only for top-model + sustained regressions where we have enough canary volume to reduce false positives, and we gate on a canary-health signal (telemetry freshness + request loop healthy) to avoid paging on broken canary. Key behaviors: 1) Severity levels: Sev2 (page) for sustained p95 latency regression OR sustained tokens/sec drop on top models; Sev1 (page) only if regression is severe and sustained across consecutive windows. 2) Attribution-friendly annotations: every alert includes model, model_version, runtime_build, kernel_tag (if present), region, hardware_sku, baseline id, observed vs baseline deltas, and deep links to the Grafana dashboard + runbook. 3) Anti-flap + dedupe: minimum sample size, sustain windows, and incident-bot dedupe keys based on (model, region, hardware_sku, signal, severity). 4) Routing: Sev2/Sev1 route to #eng-oncall and create an incident-bot thread tagged perf-canary; warning-level continues to #eng-runtime. Thresholds (initial defaults, tuned for us-east phase-1): p95_e2e_latency_ms regression: Sev2 if >= +15% over baseline for 20m AND samples >= 200 AND canary_health=ok; Sev1 if >= +30% for 30m AND samples >= 300 AND canary_health=ok. tokens_per_sec regression: Sev2 if <= -12% for 25m AND samples >= 150; Sev1 if <= -20% for 35m AND samples >= 250. Note: These are defaults; per-model overrides live in control-plane config and will be adjusted during threshold calibration. Rollout: These rules are initially scoped to top models only (via label matcher on canary_model_tier=top). They are disabled by default in non-prod; in prod they are deployed but will be set to "dry-run" (notify-only) for 48h in us-east until SRE sign-off, then flipped to paging. Testing/validation: - Unit: alert rule lint + promtool rules tests; - Integration: rendered rules in staging Grafana; - Manual: replayed recent canary time series (including known regression from SUP-3841) to confirm expected firing behavior and no false triggers on short spikes. Links: - Linear ENG-4878 (alerting policy + routing), ENG-4880 (phase-1 us-east rollout), PM-642 (rollout gates integration) - Runbook: confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-perf-regression-canary-alert - Dashboard: grafana/perf-canary/per-model (added in pr-19174) - Prior art: pr-19179 (warning-level rules) Checklist: - [x] rules have sustain window + min sample size - [x] rules gated by canary health and telemetry freshness - [x] incident-bot routing + dedupe key added - [x] annotations include dashboard/runbook links - [x] promtool tests added - [x] reviewed by SRE for paging hygiene
commits: perf-canary/alerts: add sev2 paging rules for p95 latency + tokens/sec regressions
perf-canary/alerts: add sev1 rules (high-confidence severe sustained regressions)
incident-bot annotations: include perf canary dashboard + runbook deep links
anti-flap: add min-samples and sustain windows; gate on canary health
tests: promtool rule tests + snapshot of rendered rule groups
docs: update alert severity routing notes
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): The sustain windows look reasonable, but I want a hard gate on canary_health + telemetry freshness. We had late/partial ingestion last week and I don't want pages for stale series. Also, please ensure routing is #eng-oncall only for paging; no broad channels. Allison Grant (author): Added canary_health==1 AND telemetry_fresh==1 matchers to all paging alerts, plus a "Canary unhealthy" separate warning rule (non-paging) so we still get signal when canary is broken. Routing is now incident-bot -> #eng-oncall only for Sev2/Sev1. Aisha Bello: Can we tighten the min sample size for tokens/sec? We saw variance on low volume models in staging. Also, please include baseline id + observed/baseline numeric values in annotations, not just percent. Allison Grant: Updated tokens/sec minsamples to 150 (Sev2) / 250 (Sev1) and added explicit observed_tps, baseline_tps, delta_tps_pct, and baseline_artifact fields to annotations. Rafael Mendes: Dedupe key needs to include severity, otherwise Sev1 will get deduped under Sev2 and we won't see escalation. Also confirm the incident-bot handler uses the same key. Allison Grant: Updated annotation `incident_dedupe_key` to include severity and signal; verified incident-bot expects that key (see link in description). Logan Wright: Please avoid including high-cardinality labels in the alert grouping. I see model_version and runtime_build in annotations (fine) but they shouldn't be in `group_by`. Allison Grant: Ack—removed model_version/runtime_build from group_by; kept in annotations only. Sean Gallagher: Final ask: add a "burn-in" switch to run notify-only before paging. Allison Grant: Added `perf_canary_paging_enabled` feature flag label matcher; default false in prod values; releases can enable per-region via config. Approvals: Sean Gallagher approved. Aisha Bello approved. Rafael Mendes approved. Logan Wright approved.
release_notes: Adds production paging alerts (Sev2/Sev1) for sustained perf-canary regressions on top models, gated on canary health and tuned to reduce false positives. Routes paging to #eng-oncall via incident-bot; includes dashboard/runbook deep links and improved dedupe keys.
